public_rationale: Provider announcements document a shared GPT-4o model family, and an October test supports Copilot's susceptibility to unsupported factual output. The remaining material gap is Microsoft's internal performance-review instruction at the claimed time. Microsoft's December account corroborates Connect-writing training but does not date its introduction. Partial support without contradictory evidence does not warrant a mixed outcome.
limitations: The factual-error test concerns a technical answer, not a performance review.
Shared model families do not imply identical behavior across Copilot and ChatGPT.
The evidence does not establish that employees were required to submit unverified AI output.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Microsoft asks employees to draft performance reviews from outputs of hallucination-prone generative AI models that also underpin ChatGPT.

statement.excerpt: To be extremely blunt: Microsoft is asking its employees to draft their performance reviews based on the outputs of generative AI models — the same ones underpinning ChatGPT — that are prone to hallucination.

from_speaker: based on the outputs of generative AI models
our_interpretation: The claim has three components: employee drafting instructions, shared underlying model families with ChatGPT, and susceptibility to factual fabrication.
Asking includes official encouragement or instructional guidance; it does not require mandatory use or submission without human review.
Same models means shared underlying model families, not identical application behavior, prompts, retrieval systems, or every deployed model version.
Prone to hallucination means capable of producing unsupported factual statements in ordinary use, without a specified error-rate threshold.
Use October 2024, the latest complete month before publication, for the ongoing practice.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence establishes Microsoft employee performance-review drafting instructions during the target period, use of a model family also available in ChatGPT, and that model or Copilot's susceptibility to unsupported factual output.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable evidence disproves a material component, such as showing that the alleged drafting instructions were misrepresented or that the relevant models did not share the stated lineage. Human-review requirements alone do not contradict the claim.

evidence.explanation: Microsoft publicly discussed AI-assisted employee reviews before the post. Describing an opportunity in March does not establish employee instructions in October.

Microsoft identifies GPT-4o as part of Microsoft 365 Copilot immediately before the target month. Together with e3, this documents the shared model family, but not the model used in any particular employee session.
OpenAI documents GPT-4o's availability in ChatGPT. This supports the model-family connection to e2, without establishing Microsoft's internal review instructions.

evidence.publisher: Office 365 for IT Pros — Tony Redmond
evidence.explanation: The tester reports an incorrect factual answer that persisted despite corrected source material and was unsupported by the cited records. This supports the general hallucination component only; it does not test performance reviews or isolate the foundation model as the cause.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Dated internal guidance or independently verified training records establishing October 2024 employee review-drafting instructions, with model documentation applicable to the relevant deployment.
